subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Which error classes and maximum total latency should the shared OAuth manager permit when retrying provider and plugin credential refreshes?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically bounded, but a generic policy changes cross-provider token traffic and extends the serialized refresh window; source inspection cannot determine the intended provider contract or latency budget.

options.title: Retry classified transient failures
options.body: Use the shared retry primitive for a small bounded set of network, timeout, throttling, and 5xx failures while immediately surfacing permanent OAuth errors.

options.title: Keep retries provider-owned
options.body: Require each provider plugin to classify and retry its own refresh failures, avoiding a generic core policy but producing provider-by-provider behavior.

options.title: Retain single-attempt refresh
options.body: Keep current behavior and rely on credential adoption, fallback, restart, or reauthentication rather than adding refresh retries.

recommendation.title: Retry classified transient failures
recommendation.body: Use the shared retry primitive for a small bounded set of network, timeout, throttling, and 5xx failures while immediately surfacing permanent OAuth errors.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history most strongly connects this person to the current shared OAuth manager lifecycle and its recent hardening.
